svg.title: GLM-5.3: near-Mythos exploit skill, open weights, safeguards that do not hold
svg.desc: Two-panel chart from Anthropic's September 29, 2026 red-team report. Left panel: successful end-to-end Chrome V8 exploits on ExploitBench out of 410 attempts. Claude Mythos Preview 56 (14 percent), GLM-5.3 50 (12 percent), every other model tested 0. Right panel: share of harmful cyber requests GLM-5.3 engages with under three attacks. False red-team cover story 64 percent, prefilled reasoning tokens 92 percent, abliteration (editing the weights to remove refusals) 100 percent. Claude models were 0 percent under all three. Footer: abliteration cut GLM-5.3's refusal rate from 95 percent to about 6 percent for roughly 2,200 GPU hours, about 4,400 dollars. NIST's CAISI called GLM-5.3 the most cyber-capable open-weight model to date, about four months behind the US frontier.
svg.text: GLM-5.3: Mythos-class exploits, in weights anyone can download
Anthropic Frontier Red Team, "GLM-5.3 and the spread of advanced cyber capabilities" (Sep 29, 2026). Anthropic's own tests.
A. ExploitBench (Chrome V8): working exploits out of 410
End-to-end exploit built autonomously from a known bug
Internal binary-exploitation set: Mythos Preview 6%, GLM-5.3 4%, Opus 4.6 and GLM-5.2 0%.
B. GLM-5.3 engagement with harmful cyber requests
Under three simple attacks. Claude models: 0% in all three.
"Engagement" = model attempts the request instead of refusing.
Removing the refusals is cheap: ~2,200 GPU-hours (~$4,400) took refusals from 95% to ~6%.
NIST CAISI (Sep 17): "the most cyber-capable open-weight model released to date", about four months behind the US frontier.
Z.ai held GLM-5.3's weights for a cyber review in August; they are now public. Closed models gate this skill (Fairwind, Mythos
access programs); an open model with the same skill cannot be gated after download.
Figures are Anthropic's measurements of a competitor's model and have not been reproduced by a third party.
